---
title: "Conda/Micromamba"
---

## Goals

1. Explain what a package manager and an environment are, and why projects keep separate environments.
2. Recognize how the course container, the `base` environment, and Micromamba fit together.
3. Create, activate, inspect, and remove an environment with Micromamba.
4. Record an environment in an `environment.yml` file and rebuild it from that file.

## Overview

- A **package** is a bundle of code that someone else wrote, such as `numpy` or `pandas`.
- Packages depend on other packages, and on specific versions of them. `seaborn` needs `matplotlib`, which needs `numpy`, and so on.
- A **package manager** finds a set of versions that work together, downloads them, and installs them.
- An **environment** is a folder that contains one Python interpreter and one set of installed packages.
- Different projects need different packages, and sometimes different versions of the same package. Separate environments keep them from interfering with each other.
- **Conda** is a package and environment manager. It installs Python packages, and also software that is not written in Python, such as Python itself, R, and compiled libraries.
- **Micromamba** is a small, fast program that does the same job as Conda and reads the same packages. The commands are nearly identical.
- Packages come from **channels**, which are locations that host packages. We use **conda-forge**, a large channel maintained by a community of volunteers.

## Our setup

1. The **image** is a fixed snapshot of an operating system with software already installed. Ours is Debian 12 (see [The Unix Shell](../module01/unix.qmd)).
2. The **container** is a running copy of the image. We've worked with it throughout the quarter using VSCode.
3. Inside the container, Micromamba manages a **`base`** environment with Python 3.14, Jupyter, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, matplotlib, and the other packages we have used.

The `base` environment lives in your home folder, in `~/.micromamba`.
This is why the Jupyter kernel is listed as `.micromamba (Python 3.14.7) ~/.micromamba/bin/python` (see the Module 7 [setup note](../module07/setup.qmd)).

To list the environments that Micromamba knows about:

```{text}
micromamba env list
```

To list the packages in an environment, with their versions:

```{text}
micromamba list --name base
```

To check which Python interpreter runs when you type `python`:

```{text}
which python
```

## Installing packages

```{text}
micromamba install --name base --channel conda-forge 'seaborn=0.13.2'
```

- `--name base` names the environment to change.
- `--channel conda-forge` names the channel.
- `'seaborn=0.13.2'` names the package and pins its version. The quotes stop the shell from interpreting special characters.

Common ways to write a version:

| Specification | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pandas` | Any version the solver picks |
| `pandas=2.3` | Any 2.3.x release |
| `pandas=2.3.1` | Exactly 2.3.1 |
| `'pandas>=2.2'` | 2.2 or later |

To remove a package:

```{text}
micromamba remove --name base seaborn
```

Micromamba may also remove packages that only `seaborn` needed.
Read the list of changes before you accept.

## Creating an environment

Suppose a project needs Python 3.13, `pandas`, and `matplotlib`, and nothing else.

```{text}
micromamba create --name sales-report --channel conda-forge python=3.13 pandas matplotlib-base
```

Micromamba prints the packages it plans to install and asks you to confirm.
The new environment is a folder, `~/.micromamba/envs/sales-report`.

### Activating an environment

**Activating** an environment exposes tools and packages installed to it.
For example, our `sales-report` environment has as separate `python` installation.

```{text}
micromamba activate sales-report
which python
python --version
```

`which python` now points into `~/.micromamba/envs/sales-report`, and the version is 3.13.
The packages in `base` are not available here, so `import seaborn` fails in this environment.

To go back to `base`:

```{text}
micromamba deactivate
```

Activation only affects the terminal you ran it in.
A new terminal starts in `base`.

### Using an environment in Jupyter

VS Code needs the `ipykernel` package to run Jupyter code in an environment:

```{text}
micromamba install --name sales-report --channel conda-forge ipykernel
```

Then choose the kernel as in the Module 7 [setup note](../module07/setup.qmd), selecting `sales-report` in place of `.micromamba`.

### Removing an environment

```{text}
micromamba env remove --name sales-report
```

This deletes the folder and everything installed in it.
Your own files, such as scripts and data, are not stored in the environment and are not affected.

:::::::::::::::: callout-warning
## Do not break `base`

Every note in this course assumes the `base` environment.
Try new or conflicting packages in a separate environment.
If an environment breaks, remove it and create it again.
::::::::::::::::

## Recording an environment

An environment is easy to rebuild if you write down what is in it.
The convention used by Conda/Micromamba is a file named `environment.yml`

```{text}
micromamba env export --name sales-report --from-history > environment.yml
```

`--from-history` lists only the packages you asked for, with the versions you specified:

```{text}
name: sales-report
channels:
  - conda-forge
dependencies:
  - python=3.13
  - pandas
  - matplotlib-base
  - ipykernel
```

The file is short and works on other operating systems.
Versions you did not pin may differ when the environment is rebuilt later, so pin the ones that matter.
For Python projects, pinning the Python version is usually the most consequential choice.

Anyone with Micromamba or Conda can build the same environment from this file:

```{text}
micromamba create --name sales-report --file environment.yml
```

Keep `environment.yml` in the project folder and commit it with the rest of your code (see [Git](../module01/git.qmd)).

:::::::::::::::: callout-note
## `pip` inside an environment

Some packages are only available from PyPI, the Python package index, through `pip`.
Install everything you can with Micromamba first.
Then activate the environment and run `pip` with its Python:

```{text}
micromamba activate sales-report
python -m pip install nycflights13
```

Packages installed with `pip` are not included in the export.
Add them to `environment.yml` by hand under a `pip` entry:

```{text}
dependencies:
  - python=3.13
  - pandas
  - matplotlib-base
  - ipykernel
  - pip
  - pip:
    - nycflights13
```
::::::::::::::::

## Summary

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| List environments | `micromamba env list` |
| List packages | `micromamba list --name NAME` |
| Create | `micromamba create --name NAME --channel conda-forge PACKAGES` |
| Install into | `micromamba install --name NAME --channel conda-forge PACKAGES` |
| Remove a package | `micromamba remove --name NAME PACKAGE` |
| Activate / deactivate | `micromamba activate NAME` / `micromamba deactivate` |
| Export | `micromamba env export --name NAME --from-history > environment.yml` |
| Create from file | `micromamba create --name NAME --file environment.yml` |
| Remove an environment | `micromamba env remove --name NAME` |
